text: Four signs you're being an intrusive slash clingy guy. Let's start with a simple image. You know that pushy salesman who won't leave you alone? You didn't ask for anything, you're not interested, but he keeps pitching, keeps talking, keeps following you around. At some point, it doesn't even matter what he's selling. All you want is distance. That's exactly how an intrusive man feels to a woman. And here's the important part. It doesn't matter that his intentions are good. Yes, he probably likes her. Yes, he probably wants things to work out, but his clingy behavior does the opposite. It pushes her away. So let's go through the main signs. First, body language on a date. A lot of guys underestimate this. You sit in a cafe and the man is turned towards the girl the entire date, leaning in, staring into her eyes, hanging on every word. It doesn't look romantic. It looks like an intern listening to his boss, terrified to mess up. You're a man, sit comfortably, be relaxed. Let her turn towards you. Don't make her your physical center of gravity. That already kills attraction. Second, social media obsession. You've had one or two dates, and suddenly you're fully immersed in her Instagram. She posts a story, you are the first viewer. She posts something, you instantly react. You think this shows interest. Well, maybe it does, but it also makes you look like a fan, like a salesman watching to jump in the second she opens the door. Sometimes, don't react at all. Sometimes, wait. Don't turn her social media into the center of your life. Third, texting with no balance. You send a message, she doesn't reply. There are only two reasons. Either she's busy or she doesn't want to answer. Sending another message won't magically create free time or interest. It only creates irritation and the feeling that you have no life outside of her. That's when you start looking like that clingy salesman who keeps saying, just one more thing, don't stick to her like that. Fourth, imposed help and nice guy behavior. In general, I'm not against you being a kind and supportive guy for your woman, when she's already your girlfriend or your wife, or being that guy for your friends, someone who is ready to support and help when it's needed. But early on, unsolicited help looks strange and even scary. You only met and she casually mentions her headphones broke? You don't show up to the first date with the new ones. She says she doesn't have time to cook. You don't bring her Uber Eats gift card. Nobody asked for this. It doesn't make you caring, it makes you intrusive. That's it. Good intentions don't save bad behavior. Intrusiveness is not care, it is insecurity. And the less you cling, the more attractive you become.
